# Input

23 tools for Enhanced Input actions, mapping contexts, modifiers and triggers, key mappings and force feedback.

Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_input_modifier`

*Additive.*

Reshape the VALUE a key sends before the action sees it: append a modifier (Negate to flip an axis, Swizzle to remap X/Y/Z, DeadZone for stick drift, Scalar for sensitivity) to a key mapping in a mapping context. This is how one Axis2D action serves WASD -- S is W negated, not a second action. Modifiers change the value, triggers change when it fires (add_input_trigger); list_input_types enumerates the classes, remove_input_modifier undoes it by index. The context is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_name` | string | yes | Short asset name of the InputMappingContext. |
| `action_name` | string | yes | Short asset name of the InputAction. |
| `key` | string | yes | Key name of the mapping the modifier is attached to. |
| `modifier_type` | string | yes | One of "Negate", "Swizzle", "DeadZone", "Scalar". |
| `context_path` | string | no | Asset path of the Input Mapping Context |
| `action_path` | string | no | Asset path of the Input Action |
| `key_name` | string | no | Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom) |

**Returns:** `{ context_name, action_name, key, modifier_type, modifier_class, index, modifier_count, saved, save_error? }`

## `add_input_trigger`

*Additive.*

Decide WHEN a key fires its action: append a trigger (Down / Pressed / Released / Hold / Tap / Pulse / ChordAction) so a key can mean tap-to-do-X and hold-to-do-Y instead of consuming two keys. Targets either one key mapping inside a mapping context (pass context + key) or, with no context and no key, the InputAction asset's own Triggers array -- the difference decides whether the rule applies to that binding or to the action everywhere, so a key without a context is refused rather than read as the action. The edited asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Tune it afterwards with set_input_action_trigger_behavior; list_input_types enumerates the classes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_name` | string | yes | Short asset name of the InputAction. |
| `trigger_type` | string | yes | One of "Down", "Pressed", "Released", "Hold", "Tap", "Pulse", "ChordAction". |
| `context_name` | string | no | Short asset name of the InputMappingContext. Omit it (and context_path) to append the trigger to the InputAction asset's own Triggers array instead of one of its key mappings. |
| `key` | string | no | Key name of the mapping the trigger is attached to: required with a context, and refused when there is no context. |
| `context_path` | string | no | Asset path of the Input Mapping Context, instead of context_name. |
| `action_path` | string | no | Asset path of the Input Action |
| `key_name` | string | no | Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom) |

**Returns:** `Context target: { context_name, action_name, key, trigger_type, trigger_class, index, trigger_count, saved, save_error? }; Action target: { action_name, action_path, trigger_type, trigger_class, index, trigger_count, saved, save_error? }`

## `add_mapping_to_context`

*Additive.*

Bind a key to an InputAction in a saved Enhanced Input mapping context, addressing each asset by SHORT ASSET NAME (IMC_Foo / IA_Bar) or by full object path. Returns the mapping index, which is what add_input_trigger / add_input_modifier / get_input_mapping_context (mapping_index) address. A context that already maps that key to that action keeps its mapping (added false, already_mapped true, not saved); a new mapping succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Other actions on the same key are not checked: use find_free_input_key or list_all_input_mappings first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_name` | string | yes | Short asset name (e.g. IMC_Example) or full object path of the InputMappingContext. |
| `action_name` | string | yes | Short asset name (e.g. IA_Example) or full object path of the InputAction. |
| `key` | string | yes | Key name to map (e.g. "SpaceBar", "W", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom"). |
| `context_path` | string | no | Alias of context_name, read only when context_name is absent. |
| `action_path` | string | no | Alias of action_name, read only when action_name is absent. |
| `input_action_path` | string | no | Second alias of action_name, read only when action_name and action_path are both absent. |
| `key_name` | string | no | Alias of key, read only when key is absent (same FKey names). |

**Returns:** `{ context_name, context_path, action_name, action_path (resolved object path), key, key_name (same as key), index, mapping_count, added, already_mapped, saved, save_error? }`

## `create_force_feedback_effect`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a force feedback effect asset (the controller rumble a Play Force Feedback call plays) at package_path/name, with one default channel (all four motors affected, an intensity curve with no keys, so it does not vibrate until the curve is keyed), then save it; there is no undo step. Idempotent: when a force feedback effect already exists at that path it is loaded and returned as it is, with already_existed true, and nothing is saved. An asset of another type at the path, or an invalid name, is an error and nothing changes; a failed save is an error, the new asset staying only in memory. Edit its channels and curves with set_properties (ChannelDetails) on the asset path and read them back with get_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name without folder, e.g. "FFE_Rumble". |
| `package_path` | string | no | Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/Input/Feedback" (optional, default "/Game/Gameplay"); a trailing slash is ignored. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, channel_detail_count: number, is_force_feedback_effect: bool, already_existed: bool, created: bool }`

## `create_input_action`

*Additive.*

Create an Enhanced Input InputAction asset (IA_): the verb half of a keybinding -- what the player does, independent of which key does it. Pick value_type up front (Bool for a button, Axis1D for a trigger/scroll, Axis2D for a stick or WASD, Axis3D), then bind it to a key inside a mapping context with add_mapping_to_context. Changing the type later is set_input_action_value_type; behaviour flags are set_input_action_flags. The asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_name` | string | yes | Name of the new InputAction. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Input). |
| `path` | string | no | Fallback for package_path when package_path is absent. |
| `value_type` | string | no | Value type Bool (default), Axis1D, Axis2D, or Axis3D. |

**Returns:** `{ action_name, action_path, value_type, saved, save_error? }`

## `create_input_mapping_context`

*Additive.*

Create an Enhanced Input mapping context asset (IMC_): the container that binds keys to InputActions and can be pushed and popped as a set. Prefer a context per MODE (driving, swimming, building, menu) over one key per verb -- pushing a context re-purposes the existing keys instead of consuming another global one. Empty on creation: fill it with add_mapping_to_context, and check the keys are free first with find_free_input_key. The asset is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_name` | string | yes | Name of the new InputMappingContext. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Input). |
| `path` | string | no | Fallback for package_path when package_path is absent. |

**Returns:** `{ context_name, context_path, saved, save_error? }`

## `find_free_input_key`

*Read-only.*

Which keys are still FREE: lists every input key not bound by any Enhanced Input mapping context or legacy mapping, filterable by category (keyboard / gamepad / mouse / touch) and substring, plus the matching keys that are already bound. The complement of list_all_input_mappings and the tool to run before binding a new keyboard shortcut, since a collision compiles silently and only shows up in play. Also the spelling lookup for any key the engine defines: with bindable_only=false and no category, free_keys + bound_keys together are the full engine key list, each with its exact FKey name ("SpaceBar", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom") and its display name. Trustworthy where the Python route is not: InputMappingContext.mappings is deprecated and returns empty, which makes every taken key look available.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string | no | Optional case-insensitive substring matched against the key name or display name. |
| `category` | string | no | Optional key category filter: one of 'keyboard', 'gamepad', 'mouse', 'touch'. Absent = all categories. |
| `bindable_only` | boolean | no | When true (default), only keys where FKey::IsBindableInBlueprints() is true are considered (skips AnyKey/gestures/etc.). false lists every valid key the engine defines. |

**Returns:** `{ free_keys:[{name (the FKey name binding calls take), key (same), display_name, is_gamepad, is_mouse, is_analog}], free_key_count, bound_keys:[...same shape], bound_key_count (keys bound anywhere, unfiltered), key_count (free_keys + bound_keys listed) }`

## `get_input_action`

*Read-only.*

Read one Enhanced Input InputAction asset in full: its value type (Bool / Axis1D / Axis2D / Axis3D), its accumulation behaviour, all the consume/pause/reserve flags, and the triggers and modifiers attached to the ACTION itself. The read-back oracle for create_input_action, set_input_action_value_type and set_input_action_flags, and the place to check b_consume_input -- an action left consuming input can swallow a key for the whole game. Triggers listed here are the action's own; the ones on a specific key binding live in the mapping context (get_input_mapping_context, per mapping).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_path` | string | yes | Full path to the InputAction asset (e.g., /Game/Input/IA_Jump). |
| `action_name` | string | no | Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent (short asset name). |

**Returns:** `{ action_path, action_name, value_type, accumulation_behavior, b_consume_input, b_trigger_when_paused, b_consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, b_reserve_all_mappings, trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys, action_description, b_tap, triggers, modifiers }`

## `get_input_action_state`

*Read-only.*

Read the live Enhanced Input state of one InputAction for a local player in a running PIE or game session: is_tracked, trigger_events, value, last_triggered_world_time and the mapping contexts that carry it, applied or not. It is the oracle for whether an input fired, since inject_key_input and trigger_input_action succeed either way: read it before and after, and an advancing last_triggered_world_time is the proof. is_mapped_in_applied_context false means no applied context maps it (removed on mounting, in a vehicle or a menu); is_tracked false means the engine is not evaluating it, typically an unpossessed pawn. In co-op, world picks which local player is read.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | yes | InputAction to read: full object path or short asset name. Aliases: action_path, action_name. |
| `player_index` | number | no | Local player index (default 0). |
| `world` | string | no | World selector: 'pie' (default) \| 'server' \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game'. |
| `action_path` | string | no | Alias of action, read when action is absent or empty: InputAction object path or short asset name. |
| `action_name` | string | no | Alias of action, read only when action is absent or empty and action_path is absent: InputAction object path or short asset name. |

**Returns:** `{ action_path: string, action_name: string, value_type: string, is_enhanced_input: bool, is_tracked: bool, is_mapped_in_applied_context: bool, trigger_event: number, trigger_events: array, value: array, elapsed_seconds: number, triggered_seconds: number, last_triggered_world_time: number, world_time_seconds: number, contexts_mapping_action: array, contexts_mapping_action_count: number, applied_context_count: number, player_index: number, player_controller: string, player_input_class: string, world: string, note: string }`

## `get_input_mapping_context`

*Read-only.*

Read ONE Enhanced Input mapping context asset (IMC): every action-to-key mapping it declares, each with its raw Mappings[] index and the triggers attached to that binding (the read-back for add_input_trigger and the trigger_index remove_input_trigger takes); mapping_index narrows the answer to one binding. An IMC asset stores no priority -- that is given when the context is added to a player (AddMappingContext), so it is not reported here. The per-asset reader, and the reliable one -- the Python property InputMappingContext.mappings is deprecated and hands back an EMPTY list without failing, so a scan built on it reports a fully-bound context as empty. Triggers on the InputAction asset itself are in get_input_action. Use list_all_input_mappings for the project-wide "which keys are taken / which conflict" question.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_path` | string | yes | Full path (e.g., /Game/Input/IMC_Default) or short asset name of the InputMappingContext. |
| `ctx_path` | string | no | Alias of context_path, read only when context_path is absent. |
| `mapping_index` | number | no | Optional 0-based index into the context's Mappings[] (the index add_mapping_to_context returns): only that binding is returned, even one without an action. Out of range is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ context_path, context_name, mappings: [{ index, action_name, key (display name), key_name (the FKey name add_mapping_to_context takes), triggers: [{ index, class_name, display_name }], trigger_count }], mapping_count, total_mapping_count }`

## `get_input_settings`

*Read-only.*

Read the project's LEGACY input mappings from UInputSettings: named action mappings (key + shift/ctrl/alt/cmd modifiers) and axis mappings (key + scale), each with its row count, in one call. Legacy only -- it does NOT see Enhanced Input mapping contexts, so on an Enhanced Input project it can return almost nothing while the game is fully bound. For the complete picture across both systems use list_all_input_mappings; for one Enhanced Input context use get_input_mapping_context.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ action_mappings: [{ action_name, key, shift, ctrl, alt, cmd }], action_mapping_count, axis_mappings: [{ axis_name, key, scale }], axis_mapping_count }`

## `get_player_input`

*Read-only.*

Read what a player is pressing RIGHT NOW: resolves the PlayerController for a local player index and returns it plus the currently pressed keys. Runtime state, so it needs a live PIE/game session -- an empty pressed_keys outside PIE means nothing. For which keys are BOUND (a static question) use list_all_input_mappings instead; to make an action fire use trigger_input_action.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `player_index` | number | no | Player controller index to query (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ player_controller, pressed_keys }`

## `list_all_input_mappings`

*Read-only.*

Which keys are already TAKEN, and which ones CONFLICT: aggregates every key-to-action binding across ALL Enhanced Input mapping context assets plus the legacy InputSettings action/axis mappings, and flags any key bound to more than one distinct action. Run it BEFORE claiming a new key -- a keybinding collision does not fail to compile, it surfaces weeks later inside another system. This is the aggregate you can trust: the Python route (InputMappingContext.mappings) is deprecated and returns an EMPTY list, which reads as "every key is free" even when every letter is taken. Use find_free_input_key for the complement (what is still unbound), get_input_mapping_context for one context.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string | no | Optional case-insensitive substring on the key name to narrow the returned key_bindings. |
| `conflicts_only` | boolean | no | When true, return only keys flagged as conflicts (more than one distinct action on the same key). Default false. |

**Returns:** `{ contexts:[{context_path,context_name,mapping_count}], context_count, key_bindings:[{key,display_name,bindings:[{action,source,context_path}],binding_count,distinct_action_count,conflict}], bound_key_count, conflicts:[...], conflict_count, legacy_action_mapping_count, legacy_axis_mapping_count }`

## `list_input_types`

*Read-only.*

One-call inventory of what Enhanced Input offers in this build: the four InputAction value types (the names create_input_action and set_input_action_value_type take) plus every concrete modifier and trigger subclass, including any the project or a plugin added. Run it before add_input_trigger / add_input_modifier so you pass a class that actually exists instead of guessing a name. Read-only.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ value_types: ["Bool", "Axis1D", "Axis2D", "Axis3D"], value_type_count, modifier_count, trigger_count, modifier_types: [{ class_name, display_name }], trigger_types: [{ class_name, display_name }] }`

## `register_input_key_mapping`

*Additive.*

Rebind a player-mappable Enhanced Input mapping to another key for one local player of a running PIE or game session, the way a key-rebinding options menu does (UEnhancedInputUserSettings::MapPlayerKey). It changes that player's user settings in memory only: no asset is edited, nothing is saved, no undo step. To change the key a mapping context asset declares use add_mapping_to_context and remove_mapping_from_context; back to the default key: unregister_input_key_mapping; taken keys: list_all_input_mappings or find_free_input_key. Start PIE first (start_play_in_editor): without a running PIE or game world the call is refused and nothing changes. It also needs Enhanced Input user settings enabled in the project (EnhancedInputDeveloperSettings bEnableUserSettings, before PIE starts) and a context with player-mappable keys applied to that player. A missing mapping_name or an invalid key name is an error before anything changes; when the engine refuses the remap, applied is false, success is false and failure_tags gives its reasons. player_controller and the world fields name the controller and world that were used.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mapping_name` | string | yes | Name of the player-mappable key mapping to rebind, as set in its Player Mappable Key Settings, e.g. "Jump" (required). |
| `new_key` | string | yes | Unreal key name to bind, e.g. "SpaceBar", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom" or "LeftMouseButton"; must be a valid FKey (required). |
| `player_controller_name` | string | no | Optional object name or actor label of the PlayerController to remap, e.g. "PlayerController_0" (case-insensitive), searched in every running PIE or game world; when given, player_index is ignored. |
| `player_index` | number | no | Local player whose binding changes, in the play world: 0 (default) is the first player controller, any other value matches a local player's controller id. |
| `slot` | string | no | Which of the player's key slots to set: "First" (default), "Second", "Third" or "Fourth"; an unknown name silently means "First". |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, mapping_name: string, new_key: string, slot: string, failure_tags: [string], player_controller: string, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }`

## `remove_input_modifier`

*Destructive.*

Delete one modifier from a key mapping in an Enhanced Input mapping context, by mapping_index + modifier_index -- e.g. removing a Negate that flipped an axis the wrong way -- and save the context; the call succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Indices shift after a removal, so work from the highest down. add_input_modifier is the inverse.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ctx_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UInputMappingContext |
| `mapping_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the FEnhancedActionKeyMapping |
| `modifier_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the modifier within Mapping.Modifiers |

**Returns:** `{ applied, removed_class_name, remaining_count, saved, save_error? }`

## `remove_input_trigger`

*Destructive.*

Delete one trigger from a key mapping in an Enhanced Input mapping context, by mapping_index + trigger_index -- e.g. dropping a Hold so the key fires immediately again -- and save the context; the call succeeds only when the context reaches disk. Get the indices from get_input_mapping_context (mappings[].index, mappings[].triggers[].index); they shift after a removal, so work from the highest down.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ctx_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UInputMappingContext |
| `mapping_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the FEnhancedActionKeyMapping |
| `trigger_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the trigger within Mapping.Triggers |

**Returns:** `{ applied, removed_class_name, remaining_count, saved, save_error? }`

## `remove_mapping_from_context`

*Destructive.*

Unbind a key from an InputAction in a saved Enhanced Input mapping context -- how you free a key that list_all_input_mappings flagged as conflicting, or retire a verb. Identified by context + action + key, so only the first mapping of that action to that key goes; the assets themselves survive. The engine moves the context's last mapping into the freed slot, so mapping indexes (add_input_trigger, get_input_mapping_context) can change. The context is saved, and a removal succeeds only when it reaches disk; a mapping that is not there succeeds with removed false and already_absent true, and saves nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_name` | string | yes | Short asset name of the InputMappingContext. |
| `action_name` | string | yes | Short asset name of the InputAction. |
| `key` | string | yes | Key name of the mapping to remove. |
| `context_path` | string | no | Asset path of the Input Mapping Context |
| `action_path` | string | no | Asset path of the Input Action |
| `key_name` | string | no | Input key name (e.g. SpaceBar, Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom) |

**Returns:** `{ context_name, action_name, key, removed, already_absent, mapping_count, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_input_action_flags`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set an InputAction's behaviour flags: consume_input, trigger_when_paused, consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, reserve_all_mappings, the legacy-key consume bitmask, accumulation behaviour and the editor description. Handle consume_input with care -- it is the flag that decides whether OTHER actions on the same key still fire, and turning it on can swallow the game's interaction key entirely, a failure that shows up in an unrelated system days later. Only the fields you pass change, and a call that passes none is an error; the action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Verify with get_input_action.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_name` | string | yes | Input action name |
| `action_path` | string | no | Asset path of the Input Action |
| `consume_input` | boolean | no | When set, updates the action's bConsumeInput flag. |
| `trigger_when_paused` | boolean | no | When set, updates the action's bTriggerWhenPaused flag. |
| `consumes_action_and_axis_mappings` | boolean | no | When set, updates bConsumesActionAndAxisMappings. |
| `reserve_all_mappings` | boolean | no | When set, updates bReserveAllMappings. |
| `trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys` | number | no | When set (int32 ETriggerEvent bitmask), updates TriggerEventsThatConsumeLegacyKeys. |
| `accumulation_behavior` | string | no | When set, one of "TakeHighestAbsoluteValue" or "Cumulative". |
| `action_description` | string | no | When set, updates the action's ActionDescription (FText) shown in the editor. |

**Returns:** `{ action_name, action_path, b_consume_input, b_trigger_when_paused, b_consumes_action_and_axis_mappings, b_reserve_all_mappings, trigger_events_that_consume_legacy_keys, accumulation_behavior, action_description, flags_set, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_input_action_trigger_behavior`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Tune HOW an input trigger fires on an InputAction: actuation threshold, hold time and one-shot for Hold triggers, tap release window for Tap, time-dilation sensitivity for timed ones -- i.e. how long "hold E to interact" must be held. Address the trigger either by index or by trigger_class (first of that type). Only the fields you pass change; the action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk. Add the trigger first with add_input_trigger and re-read with get_input_action.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Input Action (or short asset name). |
| `action_name` | string | no | Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent. |
| `trigger_index` | number | no | Index into the action's Triggers array to edit. Mutually exclusive with trigger_class. |
| `trigger_class` | string | no | Select the first trigger of this type (Down\|Pressed\|Released\|Hold\|Tap\|Pulse\|ChordAction) instead of an index. |
| `actuation_threshold` | string | no | When set, the base UInputTrigger::ActuationThreshold (float). |
| `hold_time_threshold` | string | no | When set, UInputTriggerHold::HoldTimeThreshold (float). Hold triggers only. |
| `is_one_shot` | string | no | When set, UInputTriggerHold::bIsOneShot (bool). Hold triggers only. |
| `tap_release_time` | string | no | When set, UInputTriggerTap::TapReleaseTimeThreshold (float). Tap triggers only. |
| `affected_by_time_dilation` | string | no | When set, UInputTriggerTimedBase::bAffectedByTimeDilation (bool). Timed triggers only. |

**Returns:** `{ action_path, action_name, trigger_index, trigger_class, properties_set, trigger, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_input_action_value_type`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change an InputAction's value type after the fact (button vs axis: Bool / Axis1D / Axis2D / Axis3D). Not cosmetic -- the type decides what shape of value the bound handlers receive and what trigger_input_action must inject, so switching it can break existing graph pins. Re-read with get_input_action and re-check the handlers. The action is saved, and the call succeeds only when it reaches disk.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the input action |
| `value_type` | string | yes | One of "Bool", "Float", "Int", "Vector2D", "Vector", "Rotator", "String", etc. |
| `action_name` | string | no | Fallback for action_path when action_path is absent. |

**Returns:** `{ action_name, action_path, value_type, value_type_set, saved, save_error? }`

## `trigger_input_action`

*Destructive.*

Inject a value for an Enhanced Input action into a local player's UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem in a running PIE or game session, so the real bound handlers run with the action's own modifiers and triggers (headless key injection never reaches Enhanced Input). dispatched true does not prove a handler fired: compare get_input_action_state before and after.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | yes | Full object path of a UInputAction, or its short asset name (required). |
| `value_json` | any | no | The value to inject, coerced to the action's ValueType: bool (Boolean), number (Axis1D), or a [x,y]/[x,y,z] array or {x,y,z} object (Axis2D/Axis3D). If omitted, Boolean actions default to true (pressed) and axis actions default to zero. |
| `player_index` | number | no | Local player index used to resolve the PlayerController (default 0). |
| `hold_seconds` | number | no | Optional float. When > 0, the value is re-injected every tick for this many seconds (so a movement AXIS actually moves the pawn), then a final neutral/zero value is injected to release. Fire-and-forget: the command returns immediately and the hold runs across the next hold_seconds of PIE. Omit (or 0) for a single one-shot sample. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). With 2+ players the default may drive the OTHER player's pawn. |
| `action_path` | string | no | Alias of action, read when action is absent or empty: InputAction object path or short asset name. |
| `action_name` | string | no | Alias of action, read only when action is absent or empty and action_path is absent: InputAction object path or short asset name. |

**Returns:** `{ dispatched: bool, note: string, action_path: string, value_type: string, injected_value: [x,y,z], player_index: number, hold_seconds: number, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `unregister_input_key_mapping`

*Destructive.*

Reset a player-mappable Enhanced Input mapping of one local player of a running PIE or game session back to its default key (UEnhancedInputUserSettings::UnMapPlayerKey), clearing the override register_input_key_mapping made for that slot; the mapping itself stays. It changes that player's user settings in memory only: no asset is edited, nothing is saved, no undo step. Start PIE first (start_play_in_editor): without a running PIE or game world the call is refused and nothing changes. It also needs Enhanced Input user settings enabled in the project (EnhancedInputDeveloperSettings bEnableUserSettings, before PIE starts). To unbind a key in a mapping context asset use remove_mapping_from_context; to see the bound keys use list_all_input_mappings. A missing mapping_name is an error before anything changes; when the engine refuses the reset, applied is false, success is false and failure_tags gives its reasons. player_controller and the world fields name the controller and world that were used.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mapping_name` | string | yes | Name of the player-mappable key mapping to reset, as set in its Player Mappable Key Settings, e.g. "Jump" (required). |
| `player_controller_name` | string | no | Optional object name or actor label of the PlayerController to reset, e.g. "PlayerController_0" (case-insensitive), searched in every running PIE or game world; when given, player_index is ignored. |
| `player_index` | number | no | Local player whose binding is reset, in the play world: 0 (default) is the first player controller, any other value matches a local player's controller id. |
| `slot` | string | no | Which of the player's key slots to reset: "First" (default), "Second", "Third" or "Fourth"; an unknown name silently means "First". |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, mapping_name: string, slot: string, failure_tags: [string], player_controller: string, world_name: string, world_package: string, world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int }`
